subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 5
summary: ICICI Times Black expands its lounge network, Standard Chartered adds a spend-based renewal fee waiver, RBL Play rewrites its welcome-benefit deadline, and two Axis commercial cards swap concierge service for golf access.
body_html:
What Changed to Your Credit Card Today?

Edition 5, 25 August 2026

If you've ever skimmed a "terms and conditions" update and closed the tab because it looked like legal filler, today's edition is proof that you shouldn't. Five cards updated their fine print in the last 24 hours, and the mix is genuinely a mix. One card got measurably better. One quietly added money back in your pocket if you spend enough. One rewrote how your welcome offer's deadline actually works, in a way that's harder to track than it sounds. And two Axis commercial cards swapped a concierge desk for a golf perk, which is either a great trade or a bad one depending entirely on whether you golf. Let's go card by card.

ICICI Bank Times Black Credit Card

The headline number changed: Priority Pass lounge access on this card went from "1,400+ lounges in 145+ countries" to "1,900+ lounges in 145+ countries." Same country count, roughly 500 more lounges added to the network.

Here's the honest way to think about that. A wider network doesn't add money to your pocket the way a cashback rate does, it adds probability. If you fly out of a mid-sized international airport that didn't have a Priority Pass lounge before, there's now a real chance it does. If you already fly out of major hubs like Dubai, Singapore, or London, you were probably covered either way and this change barely touches you.

The catch: ICICI didn't touch the part of this benefit that actually caps your value, how many complimentary visits you and your Plus cardholder get in a year. That number didn't move today. A bigger lounge list is a genuine upgrade, but it doesn't matter if you're already burning through your visit quota by October. Check your card's current visit cap before you assume this is a bigger win than it is.

Standard Chartered Super Value Titanium Credit Card

This one's a real, if modest, win. The card's renewal fee, ₹750 from the second year onward, will now be reversed if you spent ₹90,000 or more in the preceding year.

Do the math on what that threshold actually asks of you. ₹90,000 a year works out to ₹7,500 a month, which for a fuel-and-utilities focused card like this one isn't a stretch if you're using it as your main card for petrol, groceries, and bills. Cross that bar and you save the full ₹750 renewal fee, effectively making this a free card in the years you use it properly.

The catch: it's a preceding-year spend test, not a running one. If you have a slow year, a job change, a few months of lower spending, you'll pay the ₹750 without warning, because the waiver is decided by last year's number, not the one you're building right now. Set yourself a rough monthly target of ₹7,500 on this card if you want to guarantee the waiver, rather than hoping it averages out.

RBL Bank Play Credit Card

This is the change worth reading twice. The card asks you to make a purchase within 30 days of getting the card to earn the welcome benefit, that part is unchanged. What changed is the deadline for the benefit itself: it used to say "offer valid for 3 months," a flat calendar window from issuance. Now it says the benefit "shall be valid for 60 days after first statement is generated."

Here's why that's not the same thing, even though the numbers sound close. A flat 3-month window is easy to track: you know your card's issue date, you count 90 days, done. A window pegged to your first statement date depends on your billing cycle, which most cardholders don't track closely. If your first statement lands 30 to 40 days after you get the card, which is typical, 60 more days after that puts your real deadline somewhere around 90 to 100 days out, roughly similar to before, but now the exact date is something you have to look up on your statement rather than count on a calendar.

The catch: this isn't a devaluation you can put a rupee figure on, RBL hasn't published the benefit's actual value alongside this change. It's a redemption-window rule that got harder to self-track. If you've just gotten this card, the safe move is to open your first statement, note the date printed on it, and put a reminder 55 days out, don't rely on rough memory of "around 3 months."

Axis Bank Purchase Card

This is a commercial procurement card, so if you're not managing business spend on it, you can skip straight to the next section. For everyone else: Axis removed "24*7 Concierge Services" from the benefits list and added "24*7 for Golf benefit" in the same spot.

The trade is straightforward to describe and harder to value fairly. Concierge services on a business card typically cover things like travel booking assistance, restaurant reservations, and general admin help, useful if you or your team lean on it for logistics. In its place, golf access is now available round the clock instead of during limited hours, which only means something if someone on the account actually plays golf.

The catch: this is a net loss for a business that used the concierge desk for logistics, and a net gain for one where a decision-maker golfs and previously had to work around limited tee times. There's no rupee figure to put on either side here, it depends entirely on which one your business actually used. If you manage this card, ask whoever handled travel bookings on it whether the concierge line got real use before you shrug this off.

Axis Bank Purchase Control (Virtual Card)

Same swap, same day, same bank: "24*7 Concierge Services" is out, "24*7 for Golf benefit" is in, on Axis's virtual purchase control card as well. Everything said above for the Purchase Card applies here too, so I won't repeat the math.

Worth flagging separately: this update also quietly dropped the "Got more questions? Locate the nearest branch" support block from the page. That's page furniture, not a benefit change, so it doesn't get its own section, but if you were used to that page pointing you to a branch, it no longer does.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold the ICICI Times Black, this is good news you don't need to act on, just know your lounge visit cap hasn't changed even though the network got bigger.

If you're on the Standard Chartered Super Value Titanium, set a real target: ₹7,500 a month keeps you clear of the ₹750 renewal fee next year. Don't leave it to chance in a slow spending month.

If you just got the RBL Play card, don't trust your memory on "3 months." Pull up your first statement the day it lands, write down the date, and count 60 days from there. That's your actual deadline now.

If you manage either Axis commercial card, don't assume the golf-for-concierge swap is neutral. Ask the person who actually used the concierge line whether it mattered, and if it did, flag it to your relationship manager, business cards sometimes have room to negotiate what's on the account.

The fine print

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything tied to your own cards, especially a benefit change like the RBL welcome-window rewrite or the Axis concierge swap, check your bank's official notification and your card's current terms and conditions page. But here's exactly how I'd think about it.

Monzy
